title: Interruptible iterators: continuation handshake and graceful reconnect for SDKs (Python/TS/Go)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD that defines a cross-language contract and implementation guidance for interruptible streaming iterators. The goal is to provide a predictable, secure continuation handshake that allows clients to resume partially-read streams after transient network failures or client restarts while maintaining compatibility with back-level server implementations.
background: Customer reports and internal reliability metrics show that long-lived streaming iterators (chat streams, search-fanout, log tailing) are a major source of user friction when connections drop. Existing 'cursor' patterns are either heavyweight or too leaky across SDKs. We need a small, language-friendly protocol (continuation handshake) that: 1) produces compact continuation tokens, 2) negotiates token format/version, 3) optionally encrypts/verifies token payloads for multi-tenant security, and 4) gracefully falls back to stateless pagination when servers do not support the handshake.
goals: Design a continuation handshake protocol that supports version negotiation and optional token encryption/HMAC.
Provide SDK surface patterns idiomatic to Python, TypeScript, and Go for interruptible iterators that expose resume/peek semantics and integrate with existing retry/backoff behavior.
Define server compatibility rules and a fallback path (cursorless pagination or 'offset' resume) for older runtime versions.
Create acceptance tests and interop tests verifying resume across SDKs and server versions.
Document security implications and recommend KMS/HSM usage for production tokens.
Ship minimal server-side support with feature-flag rollout (canary) and monitoring for error rates and resume success ratio.
non_goals: Not implementing full transactional guarantees for exactly-once semantics; resume is best-effort with dedupe guidance.
Not changing existing streaming payload formats or higher-level API names (we aim for additive surface changes).
Not building a cross-service global token broker—token lifecycle is per-stream and short-lived.
api_sketch_python:
Proposal: expose InterruptibleAsyncIterator which implements __aiter__/__anext__ and a .snapshot() -> str method that returns a base64 continuation token. To resume: client calls client.stream(..., continuation=token) or InterruptibleAsyncIterator.resume(token). Errors: ResumeTokenExpiredError, ResumeTokenInvalidError. Example: async for msg in client.stream(...): ... token = iterator.snapshot()
Notes: integrate with existing AsyncRetryPolicy via per-chunk backoff; iterator should be cancelable via CancelledError and persist snapshot safely to disk without exposing secrets.
api_sketch_ts: Proposal: export AsyncInterruptibleIterator<T> extends AsyncIterable<T> with methods: peek(): Promise<T|undefined>, snapshot(): string, resume(snapshot: string): AsyncInterruptibleIterator<T>. Client usage: const it = client.stream(...); const token = await it.snapshot(); await it.resume(token); Behavior must be well-documented for Node/browser differences for reconnects and for streaming over fetch/HTTP2/WS.
api_sketch_go: Proposal: type InterruptibleIterator struct { C <-chan Item; Err error; Snapshot() (string, error); Resume(ctx context.Context, token string) error }. Resume should be safe to call from a different process (token can be persisted). Errors: ErrResumeExpired, ErrResumeInvalid. Use context cancellation semantics to stop inner goroutine(s).
retry_policy_spec: Clients should continue to use existing retry/backoff defaults. Resume attempts are treated as a separate call pattern: when a transient error is detected, SDK may try to obtain a snapshot and reconnect using the continuation token. Recommended server-side retry window for token acceptance: 5 minutes default, configurable per-API. For persistent errors (HTTP 4xx), SDK must not attempt resume and should surface the server error immediately.
pagination_contract: Continuation tokens are orthogonal to pagination. The continuation token must encode a minimal resume offset and a small vector of server-side acknowledgements (e.g., last sequence id), be versioned (v1, v2), and be opaque to the client. When server does not support continuation handshake (returns 501 or a specific header 'x-continue-supported: false'), clients fall back to page-based pagination: caller must request page with 'page_after' parameter and continue with stateless paging semantics.
streaming_reconnect_handshake: Handshake flow: 1) Server includes 'x-continue-enabled: v1' in initial stream response if supported. 2) Client may request a continuation snapshot via POST /streams/continuation with body {stream_id, last_seq, format: 'v1'}; server responds with token and metadata {ttl_seconds, hmac_sig_version}. 3) On resume, client reconnects including header 'x-resume-token: <token>' and server validates; if invalid or expired, server returns 440 Resume-Expired or 400. 4) Token formats: v1: base64(JSON{stream_id,last_seq,ttl,ver})|hmac; v2: encrypted blob. Security: servers must rotate HMAC keys with key IDs included in token metadata; production tokens should be short-lived and optionally KMS-encrypted. Monitoring: emit resume.success and resume.failure metrics with reason tags.
acceptance_criteria: Python SDK: iterator.snapshot() produces opaque token < 2KB; resuming with token across process restart yields continuation of stream and no duplicates beyond allowed dedupe window; tests for expired token return ResumeTokenExpiredError.

TS SDK: AsyncInterruptibleIterator.snapshot() and .resume(token) interop tested in Node+Browser environments; server non-support causes automatic page-based fallback without throwing unhandled exceptions.
Go SDK: Resume called from a fresh process leads to reconnect to the same logical stream id and continues from last_seq; context cancellation terminates underlying goroutines and returns error chain.
Backward compatibility: a server without 'x-continue-enabled' header triggers client fallback to stateless paging and logs a recoverable warning; no SDK crash or undefined behavior.
Security: token format includes key id and signature; server rejects tokens signed with revoked key; unit tests simulate key rotation and revocation.

Inter-op: end-to-end interop test where Python client writes 100 events, TS client receives first 30 then takes snapshot and resumes from token to receive remaining 70 with <=1% duplicates (dedupe tolerance), run in CI against canary server.
Observability: resume.success and resume.failure metrics are emitted; alert if resume.failure_rate > 5% for 30m on canary.
Docs: design doc, migration guide for SDK consumers, and code examples for all three languages are published in the SDK repo and Console docs.
Rollout: feature flag enabled for 1% of requests in canary region for 48 hours, then ramp plan documented and automation for rollbacks prepared.
open_questions: Should tokens be server-only and never persisted client-side in plain text by default? (privacy/regulatory implications)
What is the right default TTL for continuation tokens in multi-tenant environments? 5m, 15m, or per-customer config?
How to instrument resume deduplication at high cardinality without harming observability costs?
Do we need a signed manifest for tokens that includes allowed client_id to prevent token replay across tenants?
What's the recommended behavior when a client attempts resume against a different model/version (should server reject with 409 or attempt best-effort?).
estimates_notes: Estimate 5 points covers: design doc, API sketches and prototypes in Python/TS/Go, basic server-side stub for canary, and CI interop tests. Additional work (KMS integration and advanced key rotation) will be scoped as follow-ups.
last_discussion: 2026-03-11 meeting notes: agreed to keep token size small (<2KB), default TTL 5 minutes for GA but tunable per API; security will provide HMAC/Key-ID spec; SDKs will surface explicit ResumeToken* errors. Action items: Runtime to implement feature flag (ENG-50122), SDKs to prototype snapshot/resume APIs (ENG-51200), PM to draft migration guide.
